df["cast"].fillna("Unknown", inplace=True)
df["country"].fillna("Unknown", inplace=True)
df["rating"].fillna("Not Rated", inplace=True)

# Drop rows where date_added is missing (very few)

# Confirm no more missing values

# Strip whitespace from date_added and convert to datetime
df["date_added"] = df["date_added"].str.strip()
df["date_added"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date_added"])

# Extract useful time columns
df["year_added"] = df["date_added"].dt.year
df["month_added"] = df["date_added"].dt.month
df["month_name"] = df["date_added"].dt.strftime("%b")

# Count of Movies vs TV Shows

ax = sns.countplot(data=df, x="type", palette=["#E50914", "#221F1F"])

    ax.annotate(f'{int(p.get_height())}',
                (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2, p.get_height()),
                ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")

plt.title("Movies vs TV Shows on Netflix", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Content Type")
plt.ylabel("Count")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Build pivot table: rows = month, cols = year
monthly = df.groupby(["year_added", "month_added"]).size().reset_index(name="count")
monthly = monthly.dropna()
monthly["year_added"] = monthly["year_added"].astype(int)
monthly["month_added"] = monthly["month_added"].astype(int)

pivot = monthly.pivot(index="month_added", columns="year_added", values="count")

# Replace month numbers with names
month_names = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",
               "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"]
pivot.index = month_names

plt.figure(figsize=(16, 7))
sns.heatmap(pivot, annot=True, fmt=".0f", cmap="Reds", linewidths=0.5)

plt.title("Monthly Content Additions Heatmap", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Month")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Apply globally at the top of your notebook
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Netflix color palette
NETFLIX_RED = "#E50914"
NETFLIX_DARK = "#221F1F"
NETFLIX_GRAY = "#564d4d"
NETFLIX_BG = "#f5f5f1"

# Global plot settings
plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.figsize": (12, 6),
    "figure.facecolor": NETFLIX_BG,
    "axes.facecolor": NETFLIX_BG,
    "axes.titlesize": 16,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
    "axes.labelsize": 13,
    "xtick.labelsize": 11,
    "ytick.labelsize": 11,
    "legend.fontsize": 11,
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans"
})

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc=plt.rcParams)
print("Netflix theme applied!")

Netflix theme applied!

import os

# Create output folder for all charts
os.makedirs("charts", exist_ok=True)

def save_chart(filename):
    """Save current plot to charts folder"""
    plt.savefig(f"charts/{filename}.png", dpi=150,
                bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=NETFLIX_BG)
    print(f"Saved: charts/{filename}.png")

# Example usage — add save_chart("name") before plt.show() in every cell
In [26]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(18, 10))
fig.suptitle("Netflix Content Analysis — Dashboard", fontsize=20,
             fontweight="bold", color=NETFLIX_DARK, y=1.02)

# 1. Movies vs TV Shows
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
type_counts = df["type"].value_counts()
ax1.pie(type_counts.values, labels=type_counts.index,
        autopct="%1.1f%%", colors=[NETFLIX_RED, NETFLIX_GRAY],
        startangle=90, textprops={"fontsize": 12})
ax1.set_title("Movies vs TV Shows")

# 2. Top 10 Genres
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
genres = df["listed_in"].str.split(", ").explode()
top_genres = genres.value_counts().head(10)
sns.barplot(x=top_genres.values, y=top_genres.index,
            palette="Reds_r", ax=ax2)
ax2.set_title("Top 10 Genres")
ax2.set_xlabel("Count")
ax2.set_ylabel("")

# 3. Top 10 Countries
ax3 = axes[0, 2]
countries = df["country"].str.split(", ").explode()
top_countries = countries[countries != "Unknown"].value_counts().head(10)
sns.barplot(x=top_countries.values, y=top_countries.index,
            palette="Reds_r", ax=ax3)
ax3.set_title("Top 10 Countries")
ax3.set_xlabel("Count")
ax3.set_ylabel("")

# 4. Year-wise Growth
ax4 = axes[1, 0]
yearly = df.groupby(["year_added", "type"]).size().reset_index(name="count")
yearly = yearly.dropna(subset=["year_added"])
yearly["year_added"] = yearly["year_added"].astype(int)
sns.lineplot(data=yearly, x="year_added", y="count",
             hue="type", marker="o",
             palette=[NETFLIX_RED, NETFLIX_GRAY], ax=ax4)
ax4.set_title("Content Growth Over Years")
ax4.set_xlabel("Year")
ax4.set_ylabel("Titles Added")
ax4.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)

# 5. Ratings Distribution
ax5 = axes[1, 1]
rating_counts = df["rating"].value_counts().head(8)
sns.barplot(x=rating_counts.index, y=rating_counts.values,
            palette="coolwarm", ax=ax5)
ax5.set_title("Ratings Distribution")
ax5.set_xlabel("Rating")
ax5.set_ylabel("Count")
ax5.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)

# 6. Movie Duration Distribution
ax6 = axes[1, 2]
movies = df[df["type"] == "Movie"]
sns.histplot(movies["duration_value"].dropna(), bins=30,
             color=NETFLIX_RED, kde=True, ax=ax6)
ax6.set_title("Movie Duration Distribution")
ax6.set_xlabel("Duration (mins)")
ax6.set_ylabel("Count")

plt.tight_layout()
save_chart("netflix_dashboard")
plt.show()

Key Insights¶

Content Type¶

  • Netflix has significantly more Movies than TV Shows (~70% vs ~30%)

Genres¶

  • International Movies and Dramas are the most common genres
  • Kids content and Comedies follow closely behind

Countries¶

  • The United States dominates content production by a large margin
  • India and the UK are the next biggest contributors

Growth Trends¶

  • Netflix content grew rapidly between 2015 and 2019
  • A slight dip is visible around 2020 (likely COVID-19 impact)

Ratings¶

  • Most content is rated TV-MA (mature audiences) and TV-14

Movie Durations¶

  • Most movies fall between 80 and 120 minutes
